requirements.text: build_latest_handoff.py sets open_incidents from the last 20 incident filenames and build_operations_dashboard.py reports len(open_incidents) as the open count. With more than 20 incident files the count becomes a filename window, not unresolved state, and incidents cannot explicitly close. Add a minimal append-only resolution path that leaves incident files immutable and derives open incidents from valid resolution evidence.
An incident with a valid resolution receipt is excluded from open_incidents.
An unresolved incident is included regardless of filename order or age.
Dashboard open_count equals the number of unresolved incidents, uncapped or with an explicit truncation flag.
No incident file is deleted, moved or rewritten.
A resolution receipt that names no successful run or owner is rejected.
No workflow trigger or schedule changes.

market gates | model weights | canonical authority | portfolio logic | API budget | new policy semantics | historical artifact rewrite | threshold or anchor changes | workflow schedule or trigger changes | paid CFGI or OpenAI execution

evidence: PR #1264 merged at 139954aa556e431f8d4f5a1dff47cbe0fa2d819e after Operations Dashboard, API Agent Gateway, Storage Health, Full Architecture 1-7, Continuity Learning, Data Architecture and Automation Production Health gates all passed.

Operations Dashboard Gate run 35924605195 / job 107396566168 ran 16 tests PASS, including test_incident_resolution_is_append_only_uncapped_and_dashboard_matches and test_invalid_incident_resolution_receipt_cannot_close_incident.

The positive regression created 25 immutable incident files, validly resolved exactly one, kept all 24 unresolved paths visible without truncation and proved dashboard open_count=24, incident_file_count=25 and resolved_count=1.
The negative regression proved a receipt lacking required owner/successful-run evidence cannot close an incident and is surfaced in invalid_incident_resolution_receipts.
PR #1264 changed no workflow file; incident markdown bytes are explicitly asserted unchanged by the regression.
